chains.title: GABPA binds the alt allele and activates TERT

links.claim: GABPA is proposed to bind the alt A allele more strongly because TERT promoter mutations create a de novo ETS motif (E16a) and the GABP tetramer is reported to be responsible for promoter activation across recurrent TERTp mutations (E16b); GABPB1, the GABP co-factor, is also detected at the variant-containing element in ENCODE (E04). GABPA is chosen over other ETS factors because E16b specifically implicates the GABP tetramer. No QBiC-SELEX model/evidence is provided for GABPA, and ENCODE GABPA peaks containing the variant are only in non-glioblastoma biosamples (E17), so allele-specific GABPA occupancy at this base in glioblastoma is not directly shown.
The variant lies within cCRE EH38E3622530, a promoter-like (PLS) element with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal upstream of TERT (E01, E03).
The element is annotated as the TERT promoter, and TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0 kb from its TSS (E01, E02, E03).

In the glioblastoma DepMap expression context, GABPA is expressed (15.52 TPM, rank 303/1626) (E11), and GABPB1 is detected at the variant-containing element in ENCODE (E04), but no glioblastoma GABPA ChIP peak contains the variant (E17). Thus glioblastoma occupancy is inferred from expression plus literature, not directly demonstrated.

GABP-dependent activation of mutant TERT promoter is reported (E16b), and TERT/telomerase is associated with glioblastoma, melanoma and bladder cancer in the literature (E15); however, TERT is not commonly essential in CNS lines by DepMap CRISPR (E18), so a direct proliferation/survival phenotype in glioblastoma is plausible but not established.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP-qPCR or GABPA EMSA in glioblastoma cells shows alt > ref binding at chr5:1295113.
The alt allele increases TERT reporter activity and TERT mRNA in disease-relevant cells.
GABPA/GABPB1 knockdown or ETS-motif mutation reduces the alt-allele-specific TERT effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA occupancy at chr5:1295113 is not detectable in glioblastoma cells.
The alt allele does not increase TERT reporter activity or endogenous TERT expression in disease-relevant cells.
GABPA/GABPB1 knockdown or ETS-motif mutation does not reduce the alt-allele-specific TERT effect.

chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect at this base
predictions: Allele-specific reporter or EMSA assays in glioblastoma cells show no alt-versus-ref difference at this base.
TERT expression associates with a linked causal variant or another promoter alteration rather than this base.
No disease-cell TF occupancy difference is found at chr5:1295113.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA or other TF occupancy is demonstrated in disease-relevant cells.
The alt allele increases TERT reporter activity in a TF-binding-site-dependent manner.
Knockdown or editing of the candidate TF reduces the alt-allele-specific TERT effect.

chains.title: JUN binds the alt allele and activates TERT

links.claim: JUN is an alternative AP-1 factor proposed to bind the alt A allele more strongly at this promoter. No QBiC-SELEX model/evidence is provided for JUN, and ENCODE JUN peaks containing the variant are only in other biosamples such as A549 (E06); E04 also states that no ENCODE biosample matches the glioblastoma expression context, so glioblastoma JUN occupancy at the variant is not directly shown.
The variant lies within cCRE EH38E3622530, a promoter-like (PLS) element with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal upstream of TERT (E01, E03).
The element is annotated as the TERT promoter, and TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0 kb from its TSS (E01, E02, E03).
JUN is highly expressed in glioblastoma (91.65 TPM, rank 16/1626) (E06), but ENCODE JUN peaks at the variant are only from other biosamples, not glioblastoma (E04, E06).

If JUN occupied the alt allele, it could increase TERT expression, but the literature evidence is only general TERT/telomerase association with these cancers (E15), and TERT is not commonly essential in CNS lines by DepMap CRISPR (E18); no JUN-specific allele-dependent TERT phenotype is shown.

predictions: JUN ChIP-qPCR or EMSA in glioblastoma cells shows alt > ref binding at chr5:1295113.
JUN knockdown reduces TERT expression or TERT reporter activity from the alt allele.
GABPA/GABPB1 knockdown or ETS-site mutation does not abolish the alt-allele-specific TERT effect, whereas JUN perturbation does.
falsified_if: JUN does not occupy the variant-containing element in glioblastoma cells.
JUN binding is not allele-specific for alt over ref.
JUN knockdown does not change TERT expression or the alt-allele reporter effect.

chains.title: EGR1 binds the alt allele and activates TERT

links.claim: EGR1 is an alternative zinc-finger factor proposed to bind the alt A allele more strongly at this GC-rich promoter. No QBiC-SELEX model/evidence is provided for EGR1, and ENCODE EGR1 peaks containing the variant are only in HepG2, Ishikawa and K562, not glioblastoma (E07); E04 states that no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context, so glioblastoma EGR1 occupancy is not directly shown.
The variant lies within cCRE EH38E3622530, a promoter-like (PLS) element with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal upstream of TERT (E01, E03).
The element is annotated as the TERT promoter, and TERT is the nearest protein-coding gene, 0 kb from its TSS (E01, E02, E03).
EGR1 is expressed in glioblastoma (28.32 TPM, rank 151/1626) (E07), but ENCODE EGR1 peaks at the variant are only from other biosamples, not glioblastoma (E04, E07).

If EGR1 occupied the alt allele, it could increase TERT expression, but the literature evidence is only general TERT/telomerase association with these cancers (E15), and TERT is not commonly essential in CNS lines by DepMap CRISPR (E18); no EGR1-specific allele-dependent TERT phenotype is shown.

predictions: EGR1 ChIP-qPCR or EMSA in glioblastoma cells shows alt > ref binding at chr5:1295113.
EGR1 knockdown reduces TERT expression or TERT reporter activity from the alt allele.
The alt-allele effect is EGR1-site dependent and separable from GABPA/ETS dependence.
falsified_if: EGR1 does not occupy the variant-containing element in glioblastoma cells.
EGR1 binding is not allele-specific for alt over ref.
EGR1 perturbation does not alter TERT expression or reporter activity.

grades_v0.reason: No QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding evidence is provided for GABPA. E11 reports GABPA ChIP peaks containing the variant only in HepG2/SK-N-SH, not glioblastoma, and E04 explicitly states no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context so no peak counts as bound here. The claim that alt strengthens an ETS/GABPA site is not directly shown.
E01 and E03 place the variant in a promoter-like cCRE (EH38E3622530 PLS) with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 signal, consistent with the TERT promoter element.
E01 annotates a promoter regulatory feature and TERT upstream consequence; E02 places TERT 0 kb from its TSS; E03 lists TERT as nearby gene for the PLS containing the variant.
E11 shows GABPA expression in DepMap glioblastoma, but expression alone does not establish GABPA occupancy at this element in glioblastoma; no matching-biosample ChIP is shown.

E15 is a broad literature search with mostly unrelated titles and does not show GABPA occupancy, allele-specific TERT activation, telomerase induction, or bladder cancer relevance. General TERT/telomerase disease mentions do not support the claimed TF-mediated mechanism.

No QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific JUN binding data are provided. E06 reports JUN peaks containing the variant only in other biosamples such as A549, and E04 states no ENCODE biosample matches the glioblastoma expression context.
E01 and E03 place the variant in the PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with active promoter chromatin marks.
E01/E02/E03 assign the element to TERT, with TERT 0 kb from the TSS and annotated as the nearby gene.
E06 shows high JUN expression in DepMap glioblastoma, but JUN ChIP peaks at the variant are only from other biosamples, so glioblastoma occupancy is not demonstrated.
E15 does not connect JUN occupancy to TERT expression, telomerase activity, or cancer proliferation in glioblastoma, melanoma, or bladder cancer.

No allele-specific EGR1 binding or QBiC-SELEX evidence is supplied. E07 reports EGR1 peaks containing the variant only in HepG2/Ishikawa/K562, not glioblastoma, and E04 says no matching ENCODE biosample counts as bound here.
E01 and E03 identify a promoter-like cCRE containing the variant with active chromatin marks.
E01/E02/E03 support TERT as the nearest gene and the TERT promoter as the element.
E07 shows EGR1 expression in DepMap glioblastoma, but no glioblastoma ChIP occupancy at the variant is provided.
E15 provides no EGR1-specific or allele-specific functional evidence linking EGR1 occupancy to TERT activation and disease phenotypes.

grades_final.reason: GABP is functionally implicated by E16b and a de novo ETS motif is cited in E16a, and GABPA/GABPB1 ChIP peaks at the variant exist only outside glioblastoma (E04, E17). No QBiC-SELEX and no glioblastoma allele-specific occupancy are provided, so the alt>ref GABPA binding claim is indirect.
E01 and E03 place the variant within PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 promoter marks upstream of TERT; the element annotation directly supports the claimed promoter element.
E01/E02/E03 annotate the element as the TERT promoter and place TERT at 0 kb from its TSS, directly supporting TERT as the target gene.

GABPA is expressed in glioblastoma (15.52 TPM, E11), but no glioblastoma GABPA ChIP peak contains the variant (E17); GABPB1 occupancy is from other ENCODE biosamples (E04), so glioblastoma-specific occupancy is inferred rather than demonstrated.

E16b supports GABP-dependent TERT promoter activation, and E15 links TERT/telomerase to these cancers, but no direct glioblastoma phenotype is shown; E18 further shows TERT is not commonly essential in CNS lines, making the phenotype link indirect.

JUN ChIP peaks containing the variant are only in non-glioblastoma biosamples (E06; E04 states no ENCODE biosample matches the expression context), with no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific alt>ref assay. JUN binding at this base in glioblastoma is therefore indirect.

E01/E02/E03 annotate the element as the TERT promoter and place TERT at 0 kb from its TSS, directly supporting TERT as the target gene.

Only general TERT/telomerase association with these cancers (E15) and TERT non-essentiality in CNS lines (E18) are provided; there is no JUN-specific allele-dependent TERT or phenotype evidence.

next_experiment: The single cheapest experiment separating the top two chains (H1_GABPA_activating and H4_null_no_TF_effect) is a ref-vs-alt TERT promoter luciferase reporter assay in a glioblastoma cell line. H1 predicts the alt allele increases reporter activity; the null predicts no alt-vs-ref difference. It does not by itself prove GABPA, so a positive result should be followed by GABPA/GABPB1 knockdown or ETS-motif mutation, but it is the lowest-cost discriminator between the top two chains.
